PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Introduction to re Module

UE25CS151A
Department of Computer Science and Engineering

Prof. Kundhavai K R, CSE Department

Source slide page 2 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

re Module

The re module in Python provides support for Regular Expressions (regex). Regex is a powerful text-processing tool used to search, match, and manipulate patterns in strings. Helps automate tasks like validation, extraction, text cleaning, and pattern matching. Need not use pip install, as it is a built-in (standard library) module in Python.
A pattern defines what you want to search in text
Examples:
r"\d+" → any sequence of digits r"\b[Pp]\w+" → words starting with P or p r"\w{3}" → exactly 3 characters 
Why not use string methods?
.find() searches exact text
RegEx can match flexible patterns

Source slide page 3 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Key Metacharacters

Meta | Meaning | Example

. | Any character (except newline) | h.t → hat, hot

\d | Digit (0–9) | \d\d → 12

\w | Word character (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, _) | \w\w → hi, A5

\s | Whitespace | hello\sworld → hello world

+ | One or more | \d+ → 123

* | Zero or more | ab*c → ac, abc

[] | Character set | [aeiou] → any vowel

^ | Start of string | ^Hello

$ | End of string | world$

Source slide page 4 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Main Functions in re

re.search() → finds first match 
re.findall() → finds all matches in a list

Source slide page 5 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

re.search() Example

import re
text = "My car brand is Audi."
pattern = r"c\w\w"  # 3-letter word starting with 'c'
match = re.search(pattern, text)
if match:
    print(match.group(), match.start(), match.end())
Output:
car 3 6
.group() → actual text .start() → starting index .end() → ending index

Source slide page 6 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

re.findall() Examples

text = "My numbers: 123, 456, 789."
print(re.findall(r"\d", text))      # single digits → ['1','2',...]
print(re.findall(r"\d+", text))     # full numbers → ['123','456','789']
print(re.findall(r"\w+", "Python is fun!"))  # words → ['Python','is','fun']

Source slide page 7 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

re.sub() Example

Replace spaces with underscores
import re
text = "Welcome to Python class"
new_text = re.sub(r"\s", "_", text)
print(new_text)

Output:
Welcome_to_Python_class
re.sub(pattern, replacement, text) → substitute function

Source slide page 8 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Word Boundaries & Quantifiers

\b → word boundary 
{n} → exactly n characters 
Examples: 
text = "The fox ran"
print(re.findall(r"\b\w{3}\b", text))  # ['The','fox','ran']
print(re.findall(r"\w+ing", "learning coding swimming"))  # ['learning','coding','swimming']

Source slide page 9 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Splitting and Replacing

Splitting

text = "apple, banana orange,grapes"
print(re.split(r"[\s,]+", text))  # split by spaces or commas
Output: ['apple','banana','orange','grapes']

Replacing
text = "Password: 12345"
print(re.sub(r"\d","*",text))  # replace digits → Password: *****

Source slide page 10 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Matching Patterns

Words starting with p or P:
text = "Python programming is popular"
pattern = r"\b[Pp]\w+"
print(re.findall(pattern, text))  # ['Python','programming','popular']

Text starting with "Hello":
text = "Hello world"
pattern = r"^Hello"
if re.search(pattern, text): print("Starts with Hello")

Source slide page 11 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Emails & Phone Numbers

Find emails: text = "info@pes.edu, support@pes.com"
print(re.findall(r"\S+@\S+", text))
# ['info@pes.edu','support@pes.com']

Find 10-digit numbers:
text = "Call 9876543210 or 9123456789"
print(re.findall(r"\d{10}", text))

Source slide page 12 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING

Emails & Phone Numbers

Find 10-digit numbers starting with 9: 
text = "9000000000, 8123456789"
print(re.findall(r"\b9\d{9}\b", text))  # ['9000000000']

[00:00:00.900] Hello everyone, welcome to the session on Python modules. Today we are going to explore one of the most powerful features of Python, which is modules.
[00:00:13.796] Modules help us write a clean, organized and reusable code and then play a major role in real-world software development. So what is exact a module? A module is simply a Python file that contains code
[00:00:35.140] functions, classes, or variables.
[00:00:42.276] That we can reuse them in other programs. Python already gives us many built-in modules like math.
[00:00:52.420] OS, random and date and time, etc. That makes our life easier. And the best part is we can create our own modules. We can create our own modules and even we have third party modules.
[00:01:13.220] What are the advantages of modules? Why do we use modules? Let let's look at the advantages. First one is reusability. You write the code once and use it again and again. This saves a huge amount of time.
[00:01:28.836] Then modularity. Instead of writing code one, uh writing one long program, we break into smaller parts. Each part becomes easier to develop and debug. Next comes separate namespaces. Every module has its own space for names. So variables and functions won't clash.
[00:01:49.476] Better organization, modul us structure a project neatly, especially when it grows larger. In short, modules makes our programs cleaner, smarter, and scalable.
[00:02:06.116] Next comes types of modules. We have three types built-in modules, user defined modules, and third party modules. Let's go deeper into each of these types.
[00:02:21.124] Before that, let's see what is pip. Pip is a command to install packages. So pip stands for pip installs packages. This is a tool to install and manage the third party Python packages.
[00:02:42.500] So some of the common pip commands are pip install and followed by the package name. Then if you want to uninstall the module, you can give pip uninstall and the module name. And if you want to see what are the modules that you have installed.
[00:03:00.516] PIP list gives you a view of what all modules that you have installed. Almost every advanced Python project uses PIP. Next one is
[00:03:16.196] We'll talk about the types of modules. Built-in modules. Built-in modules come packaged with Python. You don't need to install anything, just import them and use them. So examples, math, OS, random, date time.
[00:03:33.220] These modules for everyday programming needs. So no installation is required. Next comes built built-in modules, ways to import the built-in modules. So if you want to import the entire module, you can use for import keyword.
[00:03:51.684] and the module name. In this example it is import math and then you are going to use square root function inside the math module. Import specific attributes.
[00:04:03.748] From math import square root. So in this case you need not use math.squire root. It is enough if you use square root, the just the function name. And in this case,
[00:04:14.500] When you are importing specific attributes, you can only use those specific ones which you have imported, not all of them. Importing all from math import start. This is not recommended.
[00:04:27.524] If you don't if you know the specific attributes or specific functions, please import only them, not import star.
[00:04:41.124] Then next one is user defined modules. Now let's talk about user defined modules, these modules that we create. Whenever we write a Python file with some useful functions and save it as.py file, that can be imported to another program.
[00:04:59.108] This is an excellent way to organize your own function and reuse them across projects.

[00:05:13.956] So
[00:05:16.932] Example files that you may create is you can create a.py file of any program and just you need to import use the inp keyword and import the program.
[00:05:34.084] It is the same like the built-in modules, but here you have created the own PY5. Then comes third party modules. Finally we have uh third party modules. These are created by Python community and gives us advanced capabilities.
[00:05:50.628] Okay, example like NumPai, Skycatlone, Pillow, all of them has advanced capabilities. So these modules are extremely powerful and widely used in industries and research.
[00:06:04.740] Some of the third party modules are listed down here. We have NumPy for numerical computing and we have Pandas for data analysis.
[00:06:13.572] uh or working with data sets. We have mapplotlib for charts and graphs, basically plotting and visualization. We have requests for fetching data from websites or working with APIs. We have pillow for image processing or image editing.
[00:06:29.808] These tools expand Python beyond basic programming and enable the real world application.
[00:06:37.924] So understanding the modules is essential for writing efficient, clean and professional Python code. So to summarize, modules are backbone
[00:06:48.612] of scalable Python programming. Built-in modules gives us ready-made functionality, user defined modules let us organize our own code, and third party modules bring the power of the entire Python community right into our projects. Thank you.
